STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: The shadow-DOM path hides the criteria's listed cases correctly: the nested and sibling hides, the observer on enclosing roots, restore/revert, nested calls, live announcers, row cells, and custom roots. One reproduced gap: a sibling host whose shadow root holds a live announcer is never observed, so content appended to that shadow root later stays visible, while the light-DOM analogue is hidden. The probe file is deleted and `git status` matches the start.

FILES TOUCHED: none (scratch probe `packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/zz_probe.test.js` was created and deleted)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Appended content in a non-target sibling host's shadow root is not hidden when that host holds a live announcer. Repro: `sh = host(); an = el(sh.shadowRoot,'div'); an.dataset.liveAnnouncer='true'; old = el(sh.shadowRoot);` call `ariaHideOutside([t])`, then `neu = el(sh.shadowRoot)` and await a sentinel in the target's root. `old` gets aria-hidden, but `neu` does not (`expected aria-hidden="true", received null`). Cause: the host is SKIPped because `nodeContains` sees the announcer, so its shadow root is never added to `getEnclosingShadowRoots`. The light-DOM analogue (container with a pre-existing announcer, then a later append) hides `neu` and passes.
- [minor] Hidden-by-default sibling host whose content is added later gets no aria-hidden of its own: this is the intended design and is not a finding.
- [minor] The flag-off test relies on file order (it must run before the `beforeAll` that enables the flag). It passes alone; it is order-dependent only under `--randomize`-style runs, not reproduced.
- [minor] Custom light `root` that contains no target is itself hidden. This matches the original light-DOM code path (`acceptRoot`), so it is not a shadow regression.

CHECKS:
- `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/zz_probe.test.js` (18 probes) → P1 sibling host hidden as a whole, inner content untouched, restored → pass
- P2 target host keeps its shadow content visible; light sibling hidden → pass
- P3/P4 element or live announcer appended to an enclosing outer shadow root, target two levels deep → pass
- P5 pre-existing announcer inside a sibling host's shadow: announcer visible, host skipped (light rule) → pass
- P6 append into a hidden sibling host's shadow root → no own aria-hidden → pass
- P7 light container sibling gets hidden child; light child of hidden container does not → pass
- P8 role=row sibling in shadow root: cell hidden → pass
- P9 child moved from target to shadow-root position → hidden → pass
- P10 custom root inside a shadow root → pass; P11 light root not containing host → nothing else hidden → pass
- R3 custom root = a shadow host containing the target; later append hidden → pass
- P12 revert after host removed from document: no throw, restored → pass
- P13/P14 out-of-order revert and nested calls across two shadow roots; first re-observed on revert → pass
- P15 keepVisible inside shadow root → pass
- P16 append into a target host's light DOM stays visible → pass
- P18 seeded 1000-case light-DOM differential, flag-on vs flag-off module (isolateModules) → identical aria-hidden state → pass
- R1 pre-existing announcer in a sibling host's shadow root, later append → fail (see blocking finding)
- `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays` (excluding probe) → 201/202 pass; the one failure is `useModal.ssr.test.js`, which needs `jest.ssr.config.js`; under its own config it passes (`STRICT_MODE=1 yarn jest --runInBand --config jest.ssr.config.js ...` → 1 passed)
- `yarn jest <ariaHideOutside.test.js> -t "shadow DOM is off"` → pass
- Flag leakage: the flag is set in `beforeAll` and never reset; the `shouldUseInert` block uses `isolateModules`, so no leak across files → no leak found
- PROJECT CHECKLIST: license header on the new code is unchanged; no new helper duplicates `@react-aria/utils`; the package.json dependency added `@react-stately/flags` — yarn.lock changed alongside (not re-verified with `--immutable`; the orchestrator ran the suite).

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should the sibling-host-with-announcer case be fixed by observing that host's shadow root (match the light-DOM rule), or is the shadow-root-of-a-skipped-host case out of scope for the criteria? I treat it as blocking because the light-DOM sibling behaves the other way.
